summary: Backend-only testing for K2 Life Drop. Wrote 27 pytest cases covering meta, OTP (send/rate-limit/verify/wrong-OTP), donor registration (incl. 409 duplicate, sensitive-field redaction, masked_aadhaar), public listing + filters (blood_group=B+, search=karaikal), /donors/me GET+PATCH, blood-request creation with K2-BR-YYYYMMDD-NNN numbering, GET-by-id and by-request_number, mobile filter, contact-donor flow, admin login (admin@k2lifedrop.com/Admin@123), /admin/stats (all required counters incl. donors_by_blood_group), /admin/donors (mobile/email/aadhaar_status without raw aadhaar), /admin/donors/{id}/aadhaar reveal + audit, matching-donors buckets (same_area/same_district/other filtered by Available + donation_opt_in + eligibility), notify with scope=same_area → request moves to 'Donors Notified' + notification rows created, donor-responses 'I Can Donate' → 'Donor Found', admin grouped notifications (notified/responded/can_donate), admin PATCH status → Fulfilled, user token blocked from /admin/stats (403), admin token blocked from /donors/me (403), and donor notifications feed with request details. All responses verified free of `_id` and `encrypted_aadhaar`. Fixed one critical backend bug (timezone-aware vs naive datetime comparison in /auth/verify-otp) blocking all OTP verifications. 27/27 passed on final run.

critical.issue: 500 Internal Server Error – `TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes`. MongoDB returns naive datetimes for `expires_at`, but code compared with `now_utc()` which is tz-aware. Blocked every OTP verification (user login, donor-notification tests, etc.). FIXED by normalizing `expires_at` to UTC-aware before comparison in server.py.

action_items: Review the timezone fix in /auth/verify-otp (server.py around line 450). Consider applying the same tz-normalization pattern to other places if any datetime stored in Mongo is later compared with aware datetimes (none currently found, but defensive helper e.g. `as_utc(dt)` would be cleaner).
Consider removing `dev_otp` from the response when `SMS_PROVIDER != mock` is strictly enforced in prod builds (already conditional on mock, so just verify env in prod).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~1090 lines — approaching the 700-line split threshold. Recommend splitting into modules (auth.py, donors.py, blood_requests.py, admin.py, deps.py, models.py) in a future refactor.
`last_donation_date` eligibility check uses `date.today()` (local date) which may differ from server UTC. Minor, but prefer `datetime.now(timezone.utc).date()`.
`admin_update_donor` accepts `body: dict` (no Pydantic validation). Move to a typed model for safety.
`fernet` falls back to an ephemeral generated key on bad env – silent data loss risk. Should fail-fast instead; the current .env key is valid so not hit, but defensive.
`db.otps` has no TTL index on `expires_at`; collection will grow unbounded.
updated_files: /app/backend/server.py (fixed tz-aware vs naive datetime comparison in verify_otp)
seed_data_creation: Did not reseed. Used existing 8 demo donors + created ~6 test donors (prefixed TEST_) and several test blood requests during the run; no destructive cleanup was performed (data remains for debugging).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend fully green against EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL. Run `pytest -n 0 backend/tests/test_k2_life_drop.py` (serial) – parallel execution works but hits OTP rate limit (3/10min per mobile) when fixtures share randomly-generated mobiles. The tz-fix in verify_otp is critical; without it OTP login is completely broken.
rca_of_issue: RCA for OTP 500: Motor returns MongoDB datetimes without tzinfo (naive). `verify_otp` compared `rec['expires_at']` (naive) with `now_utc()` (aware) → TypeError raised inside the handler → 500. Repro: POST /api/auth/send-otp then POST /api/auth/verify-otp with the dev_otp. Mitigation: normalize naive datetimes read from Mongo to UTC-aware before comparing with aware datetimes (patch applied). Longer-term: either store datetimes consistently as naive-UTC in handler-side comparisons, or add a small helper `as_utc(dt)` and use it everywhere.
